messages.author: 5276ff4387de2618
messages.subject: Re: Supervised analysis
parts:
Hi Edu,

Thank you for using Cardinal! For this, you will want to use the select() method in Cardinal. It works the same as the image() method, but triggers R's locator() function to allow you to select a region of interest, and then returns a logical vector indicating the selected pixels.

For example, you would do:

normal <- select(mydata, mz=XXX) # select pixels around the normal region of the image
cancer <- select(mydata, mz=YYY) # select pixels around the cancer region of the image
diagnosis <- as.character(rep(NA, ncol(mydata)))
diagnosis[normal] <- "normal"
diagnosis[cancer] <- "cancer"
diagnosis <- as.factor(diagnosis)

Unfortunately, this does mean you will need to find at least two appropriate ions (XXX and YYY) that highlight the tumor/normal regions so you can know where to select, since registration and overlay of optical images is not yet supported.

Hope this helps!

Kyle

messages.author: 5276ff4387de2618
messages.subject: Re: Supervised analysis
parts:
Hi Edu,

You're asking for sec.peaks$diagnosis before you've assigned diagnosis into sec.peaks' pixelData.

Currently, the diagnosis variable is simply a variable in your global environment, and not associated with sec.peaks. (You can still use it this way, by accessing it as diagnosis rather than sec.peaks$diagnosis.) To access it as sec.peaks$diagnosis, you must first assign it to sec.peaks' pixelData:

Either do

pData(sec.peaks)$diagnosis <- diagnosis

or

sec.peaks$diagnosis <- diagnosis # shortcut for above

before checking

summary(sec.peaks$diagnosis)

messages.author: 5276ff4387de2618
messages.subject: Re: Supervised analysis
parts:
Hi Paco. Apologies for the lateness of this reply.

You can keep re-running the select() method, and assigning them into diagnosis.

Only run *once* the line: diagnosis <- as.character(rep(NA, ncol(mydata)))

since that creates a blank vector for all your pixels.

But then you can keep re-running the select() method for each tissue and keep assigning the new diagnoses for that tissue into the 'diagnosis' vector as many times as necessary.

Use the 'subset' argument to plot the correct tissue.

-Kyle
